# docker_swarm_tokens (Ephemeral Resource)

Reads the worker and manager join tokens of the swarm the provider's Docker host manages, as ephemeral values that are never written to plan or state. Use it (Terraform 1.10+) instead of the `docker_swarm_tokens` data source when the tokens may only flow into write-only arguments (such as `docker_secret.data_wo`), provider blocks or other ephemeral resources. The host must be a manager.

Ephemeral resources require Terraform 1.10 or later. Their values are never
stored in the plan or state, so they can only be referenced from ephemeral
contexts: write-only arguments, provider configuration, other ephemeral
resources, and ephemeral variables, locals and outputs.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Join tokens as ephemeral values (Terraform 1.10+): they are used during the
# run but never written to plan or state. Ephemeral values can only flow into
# write-only arguments, provider blocks and other ephemeral resources; here the
# worker token becomes a swarm secret a bootstrap service hands to new nodes.
ephemeral "docker_swarm_tokens" "current" {}

resource "docker_secret" "worker_join_token" {
  name            = "swarm-worker-join-token"
  data_wo         = base64encode(ephemeral.docker_swarm_tokens.current.worker)
  data_wo_version = 1
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `docker_server_version` (String) Docker Engine version from GET /version.
- `engine_api_version` (String) Engine API version negotiated with the daemon.
- `id` (String) Swarm cluster ID.
- `join_tokens` (Attributes, Sensitive) The `join_tokens` structured output. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--join_tokens))
- `manager` (String, Sensitive) Token that joins a node as a manager.
- `worker` (String, Sensitive) Token that joins a node as a worker.

### Nested Schema for `join_tokens`

Read-Only:

- `manager` (String, Sensitive) Upstream `Manager`. Sensitive.
- `worker` (String, Sensitive) Upstream `Worker`. Sensitive.
